question: Why were women more common behind the camera in Hollywood in 1915 than in 1935?
answer: Because the money changed. Early film was a small, risky trade, and women wrote, directed and ran companies. In the 1920s banks and Wall Street financed vertically integrated studios, and directing became a well-paid, managerial job reserved for men. Karen Ward Mahar traces how the doors closed as the business grew.
move: When a job becomes prestigious and well paid, watch who gets shut out.
ask: In my own field, who was doing the work before it became well paid?
source: Mahar, Women Filmmakers in Early Hollywood
reference: Karen Ward Mahar, Women Filmmakers in Early Hollywood, Johns Hopkins University Press, 2006
